title: Wittmann leads from pole to win Nürburgring Race 1
dek: Marco Wittmann won Saturday's DTM sprint at the Nürburgring from pole for BMW Team RMG, 7.136 seconds ahead of Tom Blomqvist, after Lucas Auer lost the front-row start he had earned in qualifying.

chapters.title: A championship leader with 130 points
text: The 2016 DTM reached the Nürburgring for the seventh of its nine race weekends, with Race 1 the thirteenth race of the 18-race season. Marco Wittmann arrived as the leader of the drivers' championship on 130 points, having won the second race at Moscow Raceway, 12 clear of Robert Wickens on 118. Jamie Green was third on 104, Edoardo Mortara fourth on 100 and Paul di Resta fifth on 92, and six races remained for anyone who wanted to catch the BMW driver.

The field was the full 24 cars, eight each from Audi, BMW and Mercedes-AMG, each manufacturer fielding its own teams: Abt, Rosberg and Phoenix for Audi, RMG, RBM, MTEK and Schnitzer for BMW, and HWA, Mücke and ART for Mercedes. Saturday's race was the short format, 40 minutes.

One result had already been settled before a wheel turned. Lucas Auer collected his third warning of the season in Moscow, and it cost him five places on the grid at the next round. It meant that, whatever he did in qualifying, the Mücke Mercedes driver would not be starting from the front.

chapters.title: Auer fastest, but Wittmann inherits pole
text: Auer made the penalty look painful. Jamie Green had set the early target with a 1m23.161s before the cars returned to the pits for fresh tyres, but in the final dash Auer went quickest of all with a 1m22.900s, taking the best time for Mücke. Wittmann followed him over the line 0.128 seconds slower, and Tom Blomqvist, in the second RBM-run BMW, was another 0.121 seconds adrift in third.

The five-place drop meant Wittmann inherited pole position, with Blomqvist alongside on the front row and Green and Mortara behind them. Mortara had threatened to take pole himself after the fastest middle sector of anyone, but a scrappy end to his lap left him fifth fastest, 1m23.167s. Daniel Juncadella was sixth quickest for HWA, and Auer shared the third row with him, with Felix Rosenqvist seventh in the ART Mercedes.

The session showed how tight the field was: all 24 cars were separated by 0.934 seconds. Wickens was the big loser among the title contenders, only 13th, 0.488 seconds off Auer's time, with Gary Paffett one place behind him. Timo Glock, Bruno Spengler and di Resta completed the top ten fastest times, and Maxime Martin and Maximilian Götz were just outside it.

chapters.title: Wittmann gets away, Glock goes round the outside
text: Wittmann kept the lead into the first corner and Blomqvist held second, so the front of the field was left unchanged by the start. Juncadella got a very quick getaway from the third row, but it brought him no lasting gain: the Audis of Green and Mortara ran third and fourth as the field settled.

Wittmann soon began to pull clear, and the pressure behind him came from Green, who was keeping close to Blomqvist's BMW. Further back, Glock, who had been closing on Auer, braked late into the first corner and took the Mercedes around the outside; the pass was one of the better moves of the race. Di Resta, from tenth on the grid, was also working his way up and ended the race as the leading Mercedes. Not everyone got through the early laps: Adrien Tambay's Rosberg Audi was out after nine laps.

chapters.title: Mortara and Juncadella tangle in the midfield
text: The second half brought the best of the racing. Green could not find a way past Blomqvist, and Audi swapped its drivers, with Green letting Mortara through to chase the BMW. Mortara tried to get past Blomqvist under braking for the chicane; the two touched, and the Audi had to take the escape road and cut the chicane, and he gave the position back to Blomqvist.

Juncadella, who had got past Green, tried to take advantage, while Green moved ahead of him again and the fight spread over several corners. Bruno Spengler, trying to profit as well, collided with Juncadella and spun him, and Spengler was penalised for it. Juncadella fell into the pack and finished 17th, with Spengler 18th. Mattias Ekström's Race 1 ended in retirement after 23 laps, and Wittmann's lead stretched to seven seconds while the others fought.

chapters.title: BMW one-two, Green back on the podium
text: Nothing changed at the front. Wittmann crossed the line after 30 laps in 42m47.780s, 7.136 seconds clear of Blomqvist, for a start-to-finish win and a BMW one-two. It was his third win of the season and the eighth of his DTM career. Mortara made one more attempt on Blomqvist late on but could not close the gap, and on the final lap he gave third place back to Green, who completed the podium 9.031 seconds behind the winner, with Mortara fourth at 9.783 seconds.

Glock was fifth, 11.768 seconds back, ahead of di Resta and Auer, who had started the race from the third row on a penalty and finished seventh. Martin was eighth, Wickens made up four places from 13th to ninth and was only able to say after the race that something on his car might have been damaged or broken, and Götz took the last point in tenth. Green also set the fastest lap of the race, a 1m24.468s on lap six.

The result extended Wittmann's lead to 155 points. Wickens remained second on 120, Green third on 119 and Mortara fourth on 112, with di Resta on 100 and Blomqvist, who moved up to sixth, on 89. Wittmann's margin over Wickens grew to 35 points.

facts.v: Wittmann's Race 1 victory was his third of 2016 and the eighth of his DTM career.
